conventions.convention: The spacetime has signature (-,+,+,+), an independent orientation and a time orientation. Observers satisfy g(n,n)=-1; matter four-velocities satisfy g(U,U)=-c².
Use SI length coordinates x⁰=ct, electromagnetic components F₀ᵢ=-Eᵢ/c and Fᵢⱼ=εᵢⱼₖBₖ, Maxwell source sign ∇ₐFᵃᵇ=-μ₀jᵇ, and matter exchange ∇ₐTₘᵃᵇ=Fᵇ꜀j꜀.
The spatial energy-current component has units J m⁻³; physical energy flux is c times that component, in W m⁻².
Dust uses nonnegative rest-mass density ρ, j=σU and Tₘ=ρU⊗U, with σ=0 wherever ρ=0. The ratio α=σ/ρ and its transport statement are restricted to the open positive-density set.
The Ohmic relation q=χE_U, χ≥0, is an optional constitutive assumption. Nonnegative comoving electromagnetic work is a mechanical balance conclusion, without an entropy-production claim.

Killing charges use the boundary convention ∂C=Σ₂-Σ₁+B, so Q(Σ₂)-Q(Σ₁)=-Q(B). The separate probe clause requires a local potential, a symmetry compensator, finite fixed-endpoint action stationarity and ACω.

Energy conditions are pointwise tensor inequalities. DEC permits the zero current; SEC applies WEC to the trace-reversed tensor. Perfect-fluid positivity is asserted only under the displayed exact inequalities.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the smooth Lorentzian SI matter variables, dust and perfect-fluid stress/current forms, electromagnetic stress, observer fields, force density, observer energy density and spatial energy-current projection.

Adopts the smooth equation-based Einstein–Maxwell system with Tₘᵃᵇ=ρUᵃUᵇ, jᵃ=σUᵃ, ρ≥0, g(U,U)=-c², σ=0 wherever ρ=0, undivided mass continuity and Lorentz-force balance, and charge-current conservation. The ratio σ/ρ is defined only where ρ>0.

On the stated smooth coupled domain, adopts the perfect-fluid tensor, charge continuity and matter exchange, with either convective current or a specified orthogonal conduction current; q=χE_U with χ≥0 is an optional additional constitutive choice.
On an open positive-density region, dust matter exchange is equivalent to mass continuity and ρaᵇ=σFᵇ꜀U꜀. Under mass continuity, charge conservation is equivalent to Uᵃ∇ₐ(σ/ρ)=0.

The electromagnetic tensor satisfies WEC, NEC, SEC and DEC. Nonnegative dust and its sum with electromagnetic stress satisfy all four. For perfect-fluid matter, WEC iff ε≥0 and ε+p≥0; NEC iff ε+p≥0; SEC iff ε+p≥0 and ε+3p≥0; DEC iff ε≥|p|. Adding electromagnetic stress preserves each condition already satisfied by the fluid.

concerns.concern: The Example says the pure magnetic tensor “is not an isotropic perfect-fluid stress because u≠ -u,” while Verification 1.1 establishes unequal spatial stresses only in the chosen observer frame. A moving perfect fluid can also have unequal spatial stresses in another observer frame. The conclusion is correct, but excluding every perfect-fluid representation needs a short additional argument: use the zero mixed components with the perfect-fluid formula, or compare the mixed tensor eigenvalue multiplicities (2+2 here, versus a three-dimensional pressure eigenspace for a perfect fluid).

seams_checked.note: The dust and fluid postulates instantiate the independently adopted equation-based Einstein–Maxwell system with explicit matter variables, stress/current maps and equations. They do not infer a matter action or coupled existence theorem.

Dust and fluid projections preserve regularity, U normalization, source/exchange signs and positive-density restrictions. Energy inequalities retain their exact directions. Symmetry uses smooth fields, finite-chain side flux and the local-potential test-curve hypotheses; draft supplier status remains explicit.

The background postulate and source/test scaling theorem reuse the matter, electromagnetic stress and observer conventions faithfully. They separately adopt fixed-background status and do not treat the coupled dust postulate as establishing small backreaction or a coupled solution.

The counterpoised solution theorem restates the dust postulate's undivided equations, nonnegative density and zero-density charge restriction. Its fixed charge-to-mass ratio belongs to its constructed family; transport and division remain restricted to positive density.
